name: Fast Backups – Site Backup, Restore & Migration
author: Nxtapps

sections.description:
Fast Backups helps you protect, restore, and move a WordPress website. Create a complete backup in the dashboard, download it, restore it on the same site, or import it into another WordPress installation.

Visit the WPBackup.dev homepage for product information and backup guidance. Local backup, download, import, and restore do not require a Fast Backups account or registration.

A backup packages the database, media, themes, plugins, and supported site files into one portable .wpbackup file. The interface is made for site owners and developers who want a straightforward workflow without database tools or server commands.

Complete WordPress Backups

Fast Backups processes data in stages, displays live progress, and saves the completed archive in tokenized local storage. A complete backup can contain:

  • The WordPress database, including plugin and theme settings.
  • Media files from the uploads directory.
  • Installed themes and plugins.
  • WordPress content and supported files from the site root.

Restore or Migrate a Website

Restore a server backup or upload a .wpbackup file. Fast Backups validates and stages the incoming content, protects the current site’s files and affected database tables, and then applies the restore. On a different domain, it updates source-site references to the destination URL and processes serialized WordPress data.

During protected replacement, visitors see a temporary maintenance page rather than a partially restored WordPress page. If the restore fails or is cancelled after replacement begins, Fast Backups attempts to recover the original site from its private recovery copies. An independent recovery loader can retry recovery on the next request if the restore worker stops unexpectedly. A restore is marked complete only after its final verification checks pass.

Keep the progress page open until the operation finishes. Recovery needs additional disk space, database permissions, and a writable must-use plugin directory. It is not a substitute for an independent hosting or off-site backup, and it cannot repair lost disks, a lost database, or deleted recovery copies.

Imported backup archives remain available on the Backups screen after a successful import, so they can be downloaded or restored again without another upload.

Common uses include:

  • Moving a site to a new hosting provider.
  • Moving a local or staging site to production.
  • Creating a restore point before an update or redesign.
  • Recovering a site from an earlier backup.

Optional Password Encryption

Protect a backup with a password. Encryption uses AES-256-CBC when OpenSSL is available. The password is required for import and cannot be recovered by Fast Backups.

Scheduled Backups

Create independent local, FTP/FTPS, and Google Drive schedules. Run them hourly, every six hours, daily, weekly, or monthly.

For each destination you can:

  • Enable or disable its schedule separately.
  • Select how often backups should run.
  • Choose how many recent backups to keep.
  • View the last and next scheduled run.
  • Review the latest status or error.

FTP settings support protocol, host, port, username, password, remote path, passive mode, and connection testing. Google Drive supports account connection, storage information, backup runs, retention, and disconnection.

Schedules use WP-Cron and may start late on low-traffic sites. Use a real server cron job when exact timing matters.

Security and Validation

Backup work is divided into stages, and large browser uploads can use chunks when supported. Practical size limits still depend on disk space, PHP, the web server, and the host.

Security safeguards include:

  • Backup, restore, download, delete, and schedule actions require administrator capability checks.
  • Administrative requests use WordPress nonces.
  • Completed backup files use unlisted, tokenized storage paths; anyone who has a complete direct download URL can access that file.
  • Imported archives are checked for the expected Fast Backups structure.
  • Archive paths are validated to prevent files from escaping the restore directory.
  • PHP-like executable files are blocked from writable upload and cache locations during restore.
  • Backup manifests are checked before site data is replaced.

Keep at least one recent backup outside the WordPress server and test restores before an emergency.

External Services

Optional operational reporting to WPBackup.dev

Reporting is disabled by default. An administrator can explicitly enable it under Fast Backups > Statistics. Once enabled, a daily HTTPS request to https://wpbackup.dev/admin/report.php sends the site URL, plugin version, available local backup count, successful export/import/restore counts, destination schedule status, successful delivery counts and Google Drive connection status. A random installation identifier and reporting key authenticate updates. No backup contents, filenames, account emails, FTP credentials or Google tokens are sent.

Local counters remain available without reporting. Reporting can be stopped at any time; the Statistics page also offers remote deletion. Reports expire after 90 days without an update. Statistics are self-reported and may reset following database restoration. WPBackup.dev uses these optional reports for product operations and usage insights, not advertising.

  • Service: https://wpbackup.dev/
  • Reporting privacy: https://wpbackup.dev/privacy-insights.html
  • Terms: https://wpbackup.dev/terms

Fast Backups can connect to Google Drive when an administrator chooses Google Drive as a backup destination and authorizes a Google account.

When Google Drive is used, the plugin may send the following data to Google:

  • OAuth authorization requests so the administrator can grant access.
  • OAuth token exchange and refresh requests required to maintain the connection.
  • Folder lookup and creation requests for the backup destination.
  • Backup archive data when a Google Drive backup runs.
  • File list and deletion requests used for remote retention cleanup.
  • Account and storage metadata shown on the schedules screen.

Fast Backups uses the service at https://wpbackup.dev to complete Google OAuth token exchanges and refresh an expired Google access token. During these requests, authorization data required to maintain the administrator’s Google Drive connection is transmitted between the WordPress site, the callback service, and Google. The OAuth client secret remains on the callback service and is not distributed inside the plugin. The service is not contacted for local or FTP backups.

Google Drive data is sent only when an administrator connects or disconnects Google Drive, views connected account information, runs a Google Drive backup, or enables a Google Drive schedule.

Service terms and privacy information:

  • Google APIs Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • WPBackup.dev homepage

FTP and FTPS backups send the backup archive and the configured connection credentials to the server specified by the administrator. Fast Backups does not choose or operate that server. The terms and privacy policy of the selected hosting or storage provider apply.

Privacy

Local backup operations do not require external reporting. Optional daily operational reporting is off by default and only runs after explicit administrator consent in Fast Backups > Statistics. See the reporting service disclosure above.

If you configure an external destination, backup archives can contain the complete WordPress database and files, including personal or confidential information stored by the site. Make sure you are authorized to copy that data and that the destination meets your security, privacy, and retention requirements.
sections.installation:
1. In the WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for Fast Backups.
  3. Click Install Now, then click Activate.
  4. Open Fast Backups from the WordPress admin menu.
  5. Create your first backup and download a copy to a safe location.

For manual installation, upload the fast-backups folder to /wp-content/plugins/, then activate Fast Backups from the Plugins screen.

The WordPress uploads directory must be writable. Protected restores require PHP ZipArchive, private recovery storage outside the public WordPress directory, enough free space for staging and recovery copies, database permission to create and remove recovery tables, and a writable wp-content/mu-plugins directory. Password encryption also requires OpenSSL with AES-256-CBC support.
sections.faq:
What is included in a complete backup?

A complete backup includes the database, uploads, themes, plugins, supported site-root files, and a validation manifest. Plugin backup storage is excluded to prevent recursive backups.

Can I use Fast Backups to move a site to a new domain?

Yes. Install Fast Backups on the destination and import the source archive. The plugin keeps the destination URL, replaces source references in restored data and supported asset files, and safely processes serialized values.

Does a restore replace the current website?

Yes. A complete restore can replace the destination database and included files. Always back up the destination first.

What happens if a restore is cancelled or interrupted?

Before live replacement begins, cancellation leaves the existing site content in place. After replacement begins, Fast Backups uses its recovery copies to restore the original files and affected database tables. Recovery continues independently of the browser’s cancellation request. If a worker stops unexpectedly, a later WordPress request can start recovery through the independent loader.

The site remains in maintenance mode when recovery cannot finish. Keep the recovery files and database copies intact, correct the reported hosting problem, and retry. Do not delete recovery data while a restore or recovery is active.

Will this work on every PHP version and hosting setup?

Fast Backups requires PHP 7.2 or later and a supported single-site WordPress installation. Hosting limits and the requirements of the plugins and theme inside the backup still apply. Declared PHP and WordPress requirements are checked for restored active plugins and themes; importing cannot make incompatible third-party code compatible with an older server.

The protected restore currently refuses affected database views or triggers, symbolic-link content entries, linked WordPress configuration, and managed content destinations outside the WordPress content directory. It also stops when recovery storage, permissions, or free space are unavailable. These checks prevent proceeding without the recovery protection the restore needs.

Do I need to register an account?

No Fast Backups account is required for local backups, downloads, imports, restores, or FTP/FTPS destinations. Google Drive requires you to authorize a Google account. Learn more on the WPBackup.dev homepage.

Can I restore a backup without uploading it again?

Yes. Backups already listed under Fast Backups > Backups can be restored directly from server storage.

Which backup files can I import?

Import is intended for .wpbackup archives created by Fast Backups. Compatible older Fast Backups ZIP packages may also work. An ordinary ZIP is not a valid backup.

Is there a maximum backup or import size?

There is no additional plugin limit when its configured limit is zero. Hosting upload, request, memory, disk, and filesystem limits still apply. Chunked upload is used when supported.

What happens if I forget an encryption password?

It cannot be restored. Fast Backups does not store a recoverable copy of the password.

Where are local backups stored?

Local archives are stored below the WordPress uploads directory in an unlisted folder with a randomized path. Download important copies or schedule them off-site.

Are backup downloads public?

Completed backups have direct, resumable URLs so browsers and download managers can download large archives reliably. The storage directory is not listed and its path contains a random token, but anyone with a complete backup URL can download that file. Treat backup URLs as sensitive and delete server copies you no longer need.

How do scheduled backups run?

They use WP-Cron, which checks due tasks when the site receives a request. Use server cron when exact timing matters.

What happens to the local archive after a remote scheduled backup?

The plugin creates a local archive before upload. If local scheduling is disabled, it removes that archive after a successful remote upload.

Does Fast Backups support WordPress multisite?

The current public version is intended for single-site installations.

What should I check after a migration?

Check the front end, admin, theme, plugins, media, forms, and ecommerce. Clear caches and resave Settings > Permalinks if routes return 404 errors. Keep the source site until testing is complete.
sections.changelog:
1.0.195 – October 2026

  • Added local successful-operation statistics with idempotent completion counting.
  • Added optional, off-by-default daily reporting with explicit consent, opt-out and remote deletion.
  • Excluded reporting identity and consent from exported database archives.
  • Corrected database dump column lists and compatibility with legacy zero-date defaults.

1.0.194 – October 2026

  • Added staged content preparation and private recovery snapshots before live restore replacement.
  • Added rollback for interrupted restores and an independent recovery loader for stopped workers.
  • Preserved original table schemas, foreign keys, generated columns, configuration, files, and table prefixes during recovery.
  • Added preflight checks for recovery storage, permissions, available space, and declared runtime requirements.
  • Corrected server restore progress to start at zero instead of skipping the upload portion.
  • Unified export, import, and restore progress presentation and improved restore-point confirmation.
  • Prevented the WordPress session-expired dialog from interrupting server restore progress.
  • Retained successfully imported archives as reusable local backups.
  • Improved refresh cancellation, protected-file handling, empty states, and responsive admin spacing.

1.0.193 – September 2026

  • Added dynamic restore runtime protection that selects an MU-plugin guard when the web server can write it.
  • Added a database isolation fallback for hosts where PHP cannot write to the mu-plugins directory.
  • Re-applies plugin isolation after database replacement and restores only the intended activation state when migration completes.
  • Improved interrupted-import, cancellation, and failure cleanup so temporary runtime protection recovers safely.
  • Improved hosting compatibility by verifying protection from the active web request instead of relying on CLI filesystem permissions.

1.0.192 – August 2026

  • Staggered Local, FTP, and Google Drive schedule starts so large automatic backups do not compete in one WP-Cron request.
  • Added automatic retry scheduling when another export is still running.

1.0.191 – August 2026

  • Fixed secure Google OAuth broker handoffs so WordPress can validate and store the connected account without relying on a browser login cookie.

1.0.190 – August 2026

  • Added time to generated backup filenames so multiple remote-only backups created on the same day remain distinct and retention can keep the requested number.

1.0.189 – August 2026

  • Moved Google OAuth code exchange and access-token refresh to the secure wpbackup.dev broker.
  • Removed the Google OAuth client secret from the distributed plugin and from saved plugin settings.
  • Corrected the broker handoff so Google Drive returns to the current Fast Backups schedules page.

1.0.188 – August 2026

  • Preserves the source site’s custom database table prefix during restore and updates WordPress configuration to match.
  • Keeps the destination scheme, hostname, port, and subdirectory while replacing migrated URLs and serialized data.
  • Isolates migration continuation requests from restored third-party plugins until the restore completes.
  • Preserves in-flight migration state when moving between destination and source-prefixed WordPress tables.

1.0.187 – August 2026

  • Changed the Backups screen download action to a stable direct archive URL so the URL is visible on hover and web servers can handle interrupted or resumed downloads.
  • Kept the signed WordPress stream as a fallback when storage has no public uploads URL.

1.0.186 – July 2026

  • Improved the public plugin title to describe its backup, restore, and migration features more clearly.

upgrade_notice.1.0.195: Adds local operation statistics and optional, off-by-default reporting with explicit consent and remote deletion. Corrects database dump compatibility. No reporting is enabled automatically.
upgrade_notice.1.0.194: Adds protected restore recovery and fixes import/restore progress. Restores require extra private disk space, database permissions, and a writable mu-plugins directory.
upgrade_notice.1.0.193: Improves restore reliability on hosts with restricted mu-plugins permissions and safely recovers plugin activation after interrupted migrations.
upgrade_notice.1.0.192: Prevents automatic Google Drive jobs from being skipped when Local or FTP backups take longer to finish.
upgrade_notice.1.0.191: Fixes Google Drive connections returning to WordPress without saving the connected account.
upgrade_notice.1.0.190: Prevents same-day remote backups from overwriting one another, allowing retention limits to work as configured.
upgrade_notice.1.0.189: Secures Google Drive authorization by keeping the OAuth client secret on the callback service.
upgrade_notice.1.0.188: Improves cross-host migration reliability while preserving custom database prefixes and destination URLs.
upgrade_notice.1.0.187: Uses direct backup archive links for more reliable resumable downloads. Anyone with a complete backup URL can access that file.
upgrade_notice.1.0.186: Improves the plugin title for clearer identification in WordPress search and admin screens.
